item.title: The Next Big AI Debt Wave Is Pushing Credit Swaps to New Highs
item.description: Gauges of credit risk for some of the biggest technology companies hit fresh highs on Tuesday, as investors brace for an onslaught of post-earnings bond sales they fear may overwhelm already overloaded debt markets.

item.title: Maybe We Were Wrong About Blockchain
item.description: Why perps might change everything.

item.title: Netflix Looks to Bounce Back From $135 Billion Wipeout
item.description: Netflix has lost about $135 billion in market value this year with its shares down 25%. It's been making changes at the top as it tries to find some new blockbusters. Bloomberg's Felix Gillette has more on what to watch for when the streaming giant reports earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Readies China Bond Debut for as Soon as Next Week
item.description: Brazil is readying its debut panda-bond sale, which could take place as early as next week, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: GM Slides as CEO Barra Warns of ‘Intensifying’ Challenges
item.description: General Motors Co. shares fell as shareholders focused on a narrower profit outlook despite plans for another $20 billion in stock repurchases. The company now sees 2026 adjusted earnings before interest and taxes in a range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, compared with the $14 billion to $16 billion range it projected in July. Bloomberg's Craig Trudell joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trader Known for Big Aluminum Bets Is Back With Wager on Copper
item.description: A veteran metals trader known for making bold bets in aluminum has returned to the market with a major copper play on the London Metal Exchange.

item.title: Albania's Protests Pile Pressure on Edi Rama
item.description:
Albania's violent anti-government protests follow months of demonstrations against a luxury development deal with Jared Kushner.
Gresa Kraja explains the link to Donald Trump's son-in-law. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lithium Miner PLS Markets $700 Million Bond in Expansion Push
item.description: PLS Group Ltd is returning to the US dollar bond market, braving a junk-debt selloff as the Australian lithium miner lines up investments to expand production.

item.title: Carney to Unveil Budget Nov 5 As PBO Warns Oil Windfall Gone
item.description: Canada’s federal government will unveil its spending plans on Nov. 5 as the country’s budget watchdog says new measures, including a major tax incentive for businesses, will cost more than an oil-driven revenue windfall brings in.

item.title: Starboard Value CEO Jeff Smith Lays Out Case for Three New Bets
item.description: Starboard Value Chief Executive Officer Jeff Smith laid out the activist fund’s approach to its three latest investments at the annual 13D Monitor Active-Passive Investor Summit in New York today.

item.title: Canadian Dollar Hits Nearly One-Month High After Alberta Vote
item.description: The Canadian dollar posted its best day in roughly four weeks and outperformed most of its Group-of-10 peers after voters in the province of Alberta rejected the idea of separating from Canada.

item.title: Wells Fargo Indicator Flashes Buy Signal After Stock Turbulence
item.description: Wells Fargo & Co.’s sentiment indicator is giving a “buy” signal for the first time since June 2025, suggesting that US stocks have fallen to attractive levels after a slide fueled by worries over artificial intelligence and elevated oil prices.

item.title: Brokers Gear Up for Compute Futures Ahead of Regulatory Approval
item.description: Some top commodity brokerage firms are gearing up for what is promising to be the next front for AI trading: the buying and selling of derivatives tied to the cost of renting computing power used to develop and run artificial intelligence.

item.title: Treasuries Rise as Oil Retreats From Highest Levels in Weeks
item.description: Long-term Treasuries rose as benchmark oil prices retreated from the highest levels in weeks, at least temporarily allaying fears of further inflation.

item.title: Radiology Partners Pulls Loan in Sign of Market Weakness
item.description: Radiology Partners Inc. has pulled a loan offering to help fund an acquisition, the latest sign of weakness in the leveraged loan market.

item.title: Top Chicken Supplier Brazil Acts to Ease Hit From Virus Outbreak
item.description: Brazil raced to contain the trade fallout from an outbreak of a highly contagious bird disease as poultry shipments to countries including top buyer China faced restrictions.

item.title: Centerbridge, Mubadala in Talks to Buy Canaccord’s UK Wealth Unit
item.description: Canaccord Genuity Group Inc. is in talks to sell its UK wealth management business to a consortium led by private equity firm Centerbridge Partners, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Netflix Needs Blockbusters to Reverse Its $135 Billion Wipeout
item.description: Netflix Inc. needs to prove that it can produce hit movies and TV series again to stop a slide that has erased more than $135 billion in market value this year.

item.title: Gold Wavers as Traders Weigh US-Iran Talks, Fed Rate Path
item.description: Gold wavered as traders assessed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path and the status of negotiations to end the war in Iran.

item.title: S&P 500 Rises as Earnings Bets Offset Tech Swings: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks joined bonds higher as oil prices fell while bets on solid earnings overshadowed renewed tech volatility.
